verses.1: Now listen, Jacob, my servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen.
verses.2: This is what the LORD, your creator and your former, says: "From the womb, I will help you. Do not be afraid, Jacob, my servant. You are the one I have chosen, Israel."
verses.3: I will pour water upon the thirsty and streams upon the dry land. I will pour my Spirit upon your descendants and my blessings upon your offspring.
verses.4: They will flourish like greenery in the midst of water, like willows by flowing streams.
verses.5: One will say, "I belong to the LORD." Another will call with the name of Jacob. Another will write on his hand, "I belong to the LORD," and with the name of Israel he will swear.
verses.6: This is what the LORD, the king of Israel and the one who redeems Israel, says: "I am the first and I am the last. There is no other god besides me."
verses.7: Who is like me? Let someone arise and declare it, and prepare it for me. From the beginning, I have made a people to be eternal, and I will reveal things yet to come to them.
verses.8: Do not be silent or be misled. From the beginning, I have given you notice, and I have told you. You are my witnesses. Is there a god besides me? No one heard or understood.
verses.9: Those who create idols and carve them are all empty. Their idols will not benefit them. Their witnesses are themselves, and they will not see or understand, so that they may be shamed.
verses.10: Who carves a god and casts it, when it will not benefit?
verses.11: All its makers will be disgraced. Their craftsmen are from human hands. They will all gather, stand together, be frightened, and be disgraced at the same time.
verses.12: A blacksmith heats iron in the furnace, works it with tools, and fashions it with the strength of his arm. He becomes hungry, weak, and thirsty, and faints.
verses.13: A carpenter marks wood, outlines it with chalk, and shapes it into the form of a man, the appearance of a human, to be placed in a house.
verses.14: He cuts down cedar and takes cypress and oak, strengthens himself with the trees of the forest. He plants fir and rain-fed cedar.
verses.15: It will become fuel for a man, who takes some and warms himself. Over the coals he bakes bread. With it he makes fire and bakes meat. He makes an idol and bows down to it, worshipping it.
verses.16: Half of it he burns in fire, and on the other half he bakes bread. He cooks meat and eats, and is filled. He warms himself and says, "How good it is that I have been warmed, and I see the fire!"
verses.17: The remainder he makes into an idol. He bows to it and prays to it, saying, "Rescue me, for you are my god."
verses.18: They do not know or understand. Their vision is veiled, so they cannot perceive with their eyes or understand with their hearts.
verses.19: He does not consider it in his mind or know it with his understanding. He has burned half in fire, baked on the coals, and eaten meat, yet made the remainder into something detestable and worshipped it.
verses.20: He who has a heart of dust and is led astray cannot rescue his own life. Look, he will not say, "There is a lie in my right hand."
verses.21: Remember, Jacob, and Israel, that you are my servant. I formed you, Israel, you are my servant. You must not forget me.
verses.22: I have wiped away your transgressions like a cloud and your sins like a mist. Turn back to me, for I have redeemed you.
verses.23: Let the heavens rejoice, for the LORD has shown mercy. Let the foundations of the earth shout, let the mountains sing for joy. Let the forests and all trees in them rejoice, for the LORD has redeemed Jacob and Israel will be honored.
verses.24: This is what the LORD, your redeemer and your former from the womb, says: "I am the LORD who makes everything. I stretched out the heavens alone and made the earth with me."
verses.25: I will confound the soothsayers and those who practice divination. I will turn wise men backward, and their knowledge will become foolishness.
verses.26: I will confirm the word of my servant and complete the counsel of my messengers. I said, "Jerusalem will be inhabited, and the cities of Judah will be rebuilt, and their ruins will be restored."
verses.27: I said, "To the deep, be dry, and your rivers will be blocked."
verses.28: I said, "Cyrus is my shepherd, and he will complete all my desires. I said, 'Jerusalem will be rebuilt, and the temple will be founded.'"

notes:
Notes
- v. 6: "the LORD of Hosts" is retained as "the LORD of Hosts" to preserve the original compound title without altering the meaning.
- v. 15: "the remainder he makes into something detestable" reflects the Hebrew context of the idol being abhorrent.
- v. 28: "Cyrus is my shepherd" follows the Hebrew text, which uses the term "shepherd" in reference to Cyrus, rather than a metaphorical or poetic interpretation.
